reason: The sources provide sufficient details to support a short on WASP-76b with multiple multi-sourced claims.
story: WASP-76b is an ultra-hot exoplanet located about 640 light-years away in the constellation Pisces. Classified as a hot Jupiter, it orbits its host star in just 1.8 Earth days and is tidally locked, meaning the same side always faces the star. On this blistering dayside, temperatures soar past 2,400 degrees Celsius, easily hot enough to vaporize metals like iron. Extreme winds driven by the massive day-night temperature gap blow this iron vapor toward the cooler nightside, where temperatures drop to around 1,500 degrees Celsius. As the iron hits this cooler region, it condenses and precipitates down as literal liquid iron rain.
angle: An alien world where winds whip vaporized iron across the planet before it condenses and falls as liquid iron rain.

claims.claim: WASP-76b is located approximately 640 light-years away.
WASP-76b is located in the constellation Pisces.
WASP-76b is classified as an ultra-hot Jupiter.
The orbital period of WASP-76b is approximately 1.8 Earth days.
WASP-76b is tidally locked to its host star.
Dayside temperatures on WASP-76b climb above 2,400 degrees Celsius.
Metals like iron are vaporized on the dayside of WASP-76b.
Nightside temperatures on WASP-76b drop to around 1,500 degrees Celsius.
Iron vapor is detected at the evening terminator but is absent at the morning terminator.
WASP-76b was observed using the ESPRESSO instrument on ESO's Very Little Telescope.
Iron vapor condenses and rains down as liquid iron on the night side.

disputed: Distance to WASP-76b was initially estimated as 390 light-years in some older studies before being updated to 640 light-years using Gaia data. A script should use 640 light-years as established by recent data.
